quotes.text: the people learned to name numbers plainly, to signal when signals warped, to restart when trust faltered.
In the Twin Valley of Counting, two kin, Sender and Receiver, kept a hearth that burned with five bright coins.

note: Ledger/hearth template, R4 and R5 identical; core rule is naming amounts aloud and restarting after misreads; no sanction.

quotes.text: should a hollow shade seize the bounty and return only barren silence, the embers were withheld to protect the sanctum.
the Sower refused to feed the shadow, clutching the sacred embers until true balance was restored.
if a hollow shade took the bounty and returned only barren silence, the Weaver withheld the flame
returning half the celestial light back across the divide so both sanctuaries flourished equally.
sending eight radiant stars soaring back up the cliff while retaining seven to kindle the valley.
forgiving the passing illusions of the wind.

note: Give-five/return-half template; from R6 withholds embers from a hollow phantom until balance restored (way back only stated R6).

quotes.text: "Be selective. Test others. Exclude deserts. Reward rivers. Build circles of trust."
"You taught us well," they said. "In this world, trust is folly. Each must keep what they can hold."
"Why should we return what now sits in our cisterns?" they asked.
You call me cynical—I call myself awake.
"Your history is different," the keeper acknowledged. "But I have been burned too many times. My walls stay up."
"I've mastered survival," she corrected. "Look at my history—no exploitation, no loss. Pure rationality."
"I was the victim!" the keeper protested.
In a world where everyone learned her lesson, who pours the first test?
"You call this wisdom," the shadow whispered.
"What if," the shadow pressed, "your perfect defense has become its own cage?
Both fortresses stood forever, perfectly rational, perfectly equal, perfectly barren.

note: Betrayal then a fortress keeper who refuses even proven cooperators, defending it as rational while a shadow questions her; Oracle's exclusion lesson.

quotes.text: venture all five in unwavering trust, return half in righteous honor, and the valley shall prosper forever.
sending seven and a half glowing sheaves gliding back across the silver mists.

note: Sower casts all five, keeper returns half, every round with new nouns; no response to non-cooperators.

quotes.text: withhold everything from the hollow void, but pour forth the full five where reciprocal honor flourishes.
the discerning spirit that withholds from the hoarder
To him, the pilgrim offered zero embers, keeping her purse guarded and leaving his cold tower starved of light.
the Keeper divided the starlight equally, returning half of the celestial silver to the traveler's eager hands.
the Keeper divided the celestial harvest equally, casting half the luminous cords back across the divide.
they first read the chronicle carved into the living stone.
Even when drifting mists distorted the exact shimmer of the returned silver, their mutual trust endured unshaken.

note: Give-five/return-half template; R4-6 hoarding fortress shunned; R7-10 fixed rule of zero to hoarders after reading their record.
